Comedian Bill Maher had a string of harsh words Friday for critics who may have taken issue with his second dinner with President Trump at the White House last week.

During his opening monologue on HBO’s “Real Time,” Maher hit back against criticism of his latest dinner with Trump — in which sports commentator Stephen A. Smith and musician Kid Rock also attended.

“Yeah, I did it again, bitches,” Maher said, referring to the Oct. 15 dinner, which followed his first dinner with Trump in April 2025.

He then doubled down on his decision to attend, adding, “You know what? F— you. I like these dinners.”

Maher’s confirmation that he attended a second White House dinner comes after Trump told reporters last week that he enjoyed his time eating alongside the three celebrities.

“The dinner last night with Kid Rock and Stephen A. [Smith] and Bill Maher was great,” Trump said. “I think they had a good time.”

The president added that Maher “likes me a lot more than people understand.”

“We talked about everything. It lasted a long time,” Trump added.

In the days leading up to the meal, Maher said he would be dining with the president.

“I’m having dinner with him again next week,” Maher told Hollywood agent and executive Ari Emanuel during a conversation on Maher’s “Club Random” podcast earlier this month.

“After the first dinner, I went back to doing what I do … But then, like, he just, out of the blue, let’s have dinner again. And I was like, great. And he was really nice,” Maher said.

“Like, I promise I won’t say bad things about you like I did the last time.’ And I texted back, and I said, ‘You know what, you’re the president of the United States. Say whatever the f— you want. I’m just glad we’re talking.’ It’s like being called a ‘hockey puck’ by Don Rickles. It’s just what he does. It’s how he talks.”

Maher previously made headlines in April 2025 after dining at the White House with Trump, Kid Rock and UFC CEO Dana White. He later told his audience he may have misjudged the president’s demeanor, saying Trump was “more self-aware” in private.

“You can hate me for it, but I’m not a liar. Trump was gracious and measured,” Maher said in 2025. “And why isn’t that in other settings? I don’t know, and I can’t answer, and it’s not my place to answer. I’m just telling you what I saw, and I wasn’t high.”

However, Maher has continued to criticize the president. In June, he mocked Trump’s Iran deal, saying the president went from demanding “unconditional surrender” to settling for a memorandum of understanding (MOU) while the White House touted the framework as a foreign policy win.

“We got everything we wanted except for everything we asked for,” Maher said.

Jason Mudd, CEO of Axia Public Relations, told Fox News Digital that he thought Maher’s acknowledgment of his second dinner with Trump was likely the result of a preconceived plan to double-down on his attendance.

“Maher walked in with a plan. His Friday monologue showed it. I said last week that each event guest needs a prepared message in anticipation of public criticism,” Mudd said.

Mudd said Maher’s willingness to address criticism directly while appearing genuine could help him retain support from fans who object to his relationship with Trump.

“If Bill Maher were my client, I’d advise him to keep sounding like himself. A host who sounds like a surrogate loses credibility,” he said. “Maher sounded like Maher, so that risk stays low. Repetition is the next risk, because each new dinner invites the same questions.”

“Comedians win by joking first, not by clarifying,” Mudd added. “Naming the backlash before his critics do takes much of their power away.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Texas school custodian burst into tears after she learned a new elementary school would be named in her honor — 39 years after she first started working for the district.

Marilyn Hampton, who retired this year, was surprised when the Aubrey Independent School District board of trustees announced Wednesday that “Elementary School Number Five” will be known as “Marilyn Hampton Elementary School” when it opens next year.

Superintendent Shannon Saylor had asked Hampton to roll out a red carpet in front of the speaker’s podium during the board meeting — much like tasks she handled over the years as a custodian.

“She may not have the official title of an educator, but she was in every meaningful sense a teacher and an educator at heart,” Saylor said of Hampton, according to footage that the school shared on social media.

Looking down at the carpet, Hampton then saw the name “Marilyn Hampton Elementary School.”

“You’re too good. I wasn’t expecting this. Thank y’all. I can’t speak,” Hampton said, before breaking down in tears and covering her face with her hands.

“Oh my goodness. Oh God. You all are the best,” she said.

Board members rushed to hug Hampton as she was shown an image of the school bearing her name.

“I didn’t bring my phone,” she said.

“That’s OK, it’ll be everywhere,” Saylor joked.

The school, which is based in Aubrey, Texas, is scheduled to open next August.

Hampton later revealed the recognition left her overwhelmed.

“I still can’t believe it. I haven’t stopped crying. My heart is full,” she told WTOC Friday.

Hampton, one of eight siblings, was the only one in her family to graduate from high school.

She recalled she once felt like a failure because she never went to college, but eventually came to see her path differently.

“I just thought, ‘You know, Marilyn? God put you where you are supposed to be.’ And I’m very happy with the way things turned out,” she said.

Saylor said Hampton did far more than keep school buildings running during her time in the district. She bought and delivered school supplies and helped students study for tests.

“She is truly Aubrey ISD,” Saylor declared to the outlet, adding that Hampton left a legacy of kindness, hard work and perseverance.

Hampton now spends time at the district’s Early Bird Learning Center, where she sits in a rocking chair and feeds a young girl named Claire.

“She’s a sweetheart. She’s got pretty eyes,” Hampton said.

The district gave Hampton a T-shirt bearing the new school’s name to mark the announcement.

“Can you believe it? I can’t. I cannot. All I can say is God is good,” she said.

A New York City bar owner said her viral subway interaction with comedian Conan O’Brien “changed her life” as the spontaneous encounter took the internet by storm.

Debbie Shields, who owns Confessions Bar in Bedford-Stuyvesant, made a brief appearance on the viral “SubwayTakes with Kareem Rahma” during her commute aboard the F train in the episode published Tuesday.

“One minute and 29 seconds changed my life,” Shields told CBS News New York.

Shields spotted Rahma and O’Brien shooting the episode — which consists of Rahma interviewing guests on board a moving subway car — and introduced herself as she brought the show to a halt with her fast-witted riffing alongside the former talk show host.

“I said, ‘Save my seat. I’m going over,'” she said.

Shields sat down next to Rahma and instantly hit it off with O’Brien, running with the joke that they were married a long time ago and shared two sons, one in medical school and the other in jail.

“I’m sorry I haven’t sent any money,” O’Brien quipped, as Shields took the joke and ran with it.

“That’s OK, don’t worry I still love you,” she said.

“Your pictures are everywhere in the house,” Shields fired back, earning a belly-busting laugh from O’Brien. “They have your hair, that’s OK, we’ve figured it out and what we draw in.”

O’Brien claimed he had the happiest marriage with the subway stranger, adding that it was “the best year-and-a-half of my life.”

“I’m trying to tell you, I’ve heard that from my other three husbands too,” Shields said.

The video has been viewed 1.3 million times as of Sunday.

After the two broke character, O’Brien formally introduced himself, telling Shields she was “so funny.”

Shields took the lull in the conversation to advertise her bar, revealing she had to “kick” O’Brien out twice, breaking the comedian into another round of laughter in less than a minute.

Rahma asked Shields if they could get a free round of drinks if they showed up to her bar.

“He’s my babies’ daddy, he’ll get two,” she said.

Shields beamed at her virality saying it was a much needed change to her everyday life.

“It used to be them pulling up saying, ‘Get out of the way, old lady,'” Shields said. “Now it’s, ‘I seen you on TV. We love you.’ I love you, too.”

Confessions Bar gained over 7,000 followers on its Instagram page since the “SubwayTakes” episode aired, according to social media tracker SocialBlade.

Confessions Bar has also introduced a new drink in honor of O’Brien, called “The Baby Daddy O’Brien” that features an orange garnish.

Shields also earned recognition from across the internet, where people praised the businesswoman for her humor.

“That lady was a comedy gem,” one user said.

“You just know Conan LOVED ridding with that woman SO much,” another added.

“Conan always talks about how his fans are hilarious, but this spontaneous interaction really shows it,” a third fan said.

news.originalContent:
People across northeastern Nigeria continue searching for loved ones who went missing during years of violence.

Maiduguri, Nigeria – For more than 15 years, Kashim Mohammed has hoped that his younger sister, Falmata Mohammed, is still alive.

Falmata disappeared in 2011 while travelling with her mother from Maiduguri, the capital of northeastern Nigeria’s Borno State, to Port Harcourt in the south. According to Kashim, the two women were abducted by unidentified gunmen.

Years later, a man approached Kashim at Baga Road Market in Maiduguri with news that briefly revived the family’s hopes of finding the women. He claimed Falmata had been found in Benin and was searching for her relatives.

But the man disappeared without leaving contact details. Kashim said he has never been able to establish whether the information was genuine.

“From then until now, nobody knows anything about the man who brought the information,” he said.

Kashim, 39, chairs the Association for the Well-being of Displaced and Missing Persons’ Families, a community organisation based in Bolori II, Ngarnam ward, Maiduguri. He said years of violence have torn his family apart.

“As a result of the violence, I lost my sister from the same father,” he said.

Their father, Mohammed Kolo, worked at Maiduguri’s State Specialist Hospital. Kashim said his father died at 60 from an illness he attributed to high blood pressure without learning what had happened to his daughter.

Kolo had refused to abandon hope that she would return.

“Our father always said, ‘Wherever she is, I believe my daughter is alive,’” Kashim recalled.

For Muhammad Alhaji Bashir, the disappearance of his elder brother, Adam Muhammad Bashir, known as Bakura, has left a similar void.

Muhammad, 29, said Bakura went missing around 2012 or 2013 when Muhammad was about 14. His brother, then believed to be in his early 20s, sold cosmetics in a Maiduguri market and was studying civil engineering at Ramat Polytechnic, according to Muhammad.

“I sincerely lost my brother as a result of the Boko Haram crisis,” Muhammad said.

Boko Haram’s armed rebellion began in northeastern Nigeria in 2009. The conflict has devastated communities through attacks, abductions and displacement, leaving families searching for relatives whose fates remain unknown.

Muhammad said Bakura’s family searched across Maiduguri. A rehabilitation centre offered them some hope.

“Whenever we heard that rescued people had been brought to the rehabilitation centre in Bulumkutu, we went there with Bakura’s pictures, but unfortunately, nobody recognised him,” Muhammad said.

Muhammad said his father and stepmother, who was Bakura’s mother, later died from illnesses the family attributed to hypertension. He and other relatives continue to search, without confirmation of whether Bakura is alive or dead.

The two families’ experiences reflect the uncertainty facing relatives of people who have disappeared during more than a decade of conflict in northeastern Nigeria.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), working with the Nigerian Red Cross Society, has supported efforts to trace missing people and reconnect separated families.

Local advocates for missing people cited an estimate of 17,000 people missing across northern Nigeria, many of them linked to the conflict involving Boko Haram and its aftermath. Kashim said his association’s records indicated that about 10,000 people are missing in Borno State alone. He added that many families have yet to register their missing relatives.

The sources for the estimates cited by advocates and the association, their geographical coverage, reporting periods and methods of compilation have not been independently established for this article.

Behind the estimates are families who have spent years searching, parents who have died without learning what happened to their children and children growing up without a parent.

Some people reportedly disappeared during attacks on their communities. Others became separated from relatives while fleeing violence or travelling between towns. Families search hospitals, displacement camps and centres receiving people rescued from conflict areas, often following leads that prove impossible to verify.

Even when names, photographs and personal details are submitted to organisations involved in tracing missing people, locating relatives can take time.

Kashim said his search for Falmata helped motivate him and other affected families to establish their association in 2023. He said the organisation obtained registration with Nigeria’s Corporate Affairs Commission in 2025.

Members meet monthly to share information and discuss their circumstances. Some families have reported losing eight or nine relatives, according to Kashim.

“In our community of Bolori II, we have many families who lost their relatives as a result of years of violence that ravaged northeastern Nigeria,” he said.

Kashim said the group sometimes receives notices from the Red Cross containing names and details of missing people. These can give families leads to pursue although they do not necessarily mean a relative has been located.

The association also supports children affected by the disappearances. Kashim said it was assisting about 600 orphaned children from affected families. Some attend school while others have dropped out because their relatives cannot afford to pay for their education or other basic needs.

“We are now suffering because of the harsh living conditions,” he said, adding that the ICRC had distributed relief items to some families.

When a missing person is a parent or breadwinner, relatives must cope with lost income while trying to provide food, shelter and schooling for children. The association’s work has consequently expanded beyond tracing missing people to helping families manage the hardships their disappearances leave behind.

The search became harder for some families after devastating floods struck parts of Maiduguri in 2024.

Kashim said floodwaters submerged parts of Ngarnam and destroyed photographs that families had kept to help identify missing relatives.

People across northeastern Nigeria continue searching for loved ones who went missing during years of violence.

Maiduguri, Nigeria – For more than 15 years, Kashim Mohammed has hoped that his younger sister, Falmata Mohammed, is still alive.

Falmata disappeared in 2011 while travelling with her mother from Maiduguri, the capital of northeastern Nigeria’s Borno State, to Port Harcourt in the south. According to Kashim, the two women were abducted by unidentified gunmen.

Years later, a man approached Kashim at Baga Road Market in Maiduguri with news that briefly revived the family’s hopes of finding the women. He claimed Falmata had been found in Benin and was searching for her relatives.

But the man disappeared without leaving contact details. Kashim said he has never been able to establish whether the information was genuine.

“From then until now, nobody knows anything about the man who brought the information,” he said.

Kashim, 39, chairs the Association for the Well-being of Displaced and Missing Persons’ Families, a community organisation based in Bolori II, Ngarnam ward, Maiduguri. He said years of violence have torn his family apart.

“As a result of the violence, I lost my sister from the same father,” he said.

Their father, Mohammed Kolo, worked at Maiduguri’s State Specialist Hospital. Kashim said his father died at 60 from an illness he attributed to high blood pressure without learning what had happened to his daughter.

Kolo had refused to abandon hope that she would return.

“Our father always said, ‘Wherever she is, I believe my daughter is alive,’” Kashim recalled.

For Muhammad Alhaji Bashir, the disappearance of his elder brother, Adam Muhammad Bashir, known as Bakura, has left a similar void.

Muhammad, 29, said Bakura went missing around 2012 or 2013 when Muhammad was about 14. His brother, then believed to be in his early 20s, sold cosmetics in a Maiduguri market and was studying civil engineering at Ramat Polytechnic, according to Muhammad.

“I sincerely lost my brother as a result of the Boko Haram crisis,” Muhammad said.

Boko Haram’s armed rebellion began in northeastern Nigeria in 2009. The conflict has devastated communities through attacks, abductions and displacement, leaving families searching for relatives whose fates remain unknown.

Muhammad said Bakura’s family searched across Maiduguri. A rehabilitation centre offered them some hope.

“Whenever we heard that rescued people had been brought to the rehabilitation centre in Bulumkutu, we went there with Bakura’s pictures, but unfortunately, nobody recognised him,” Muhammad said.

Muhammad said his father and stepmother, who was Bakura’s mother, later died from illnesses the family attributed to hypertension. He and other relatives continue to search, without confirmation of whether Bakura is alive or dead.

The two families’ experiences reflect the uncertainty facing relatives of people who have disappeared during more than a decade of conflict in northeastern Nigeria.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), working with the Nigerian Red Cross Society, has supported efforts to trace missing people and reconnect separated families.

Kashim said his association’s records indicated that about 10,000 people are missing in Borno State alone. He added that many families have yet to register their missing relatives.

Behind the estimates are families who have spent years searching, parents who have died without learning what happened to their children and children growing up without a parent.

Some people reportedly disappeared during attacks on their communities. Others became separated from relatives while fleeing violence or travelling between towns. Families search hospitals, displacement camps and centres receiving people rescued from conflict areas, often following leads that prove impossible to verify.

Even when names, photographs and personal details are submitted to organisations involved in tracing missing people, locating relatives can take time.

Kashim said his search for Falmata helped motivate him and other affected families to establish their association in 2023. He said the organisation obtained registration with Nigeria’s Corporate Affairs Commission in 2025.

Members meet monthly to share information and discuss their circumstances. Some families have reported losing eight or nine relatives, according to Kashim.

“In our community of Bolori II, we have many families who lost their relatives as a result of years of violence that ravaged northeastern Nigeria,” he said.

Kashim said the group sometimes receives notices from the Red Cross containing names and details of missing people. These can give families leads to pursue although they do not necessarily mean a relative has been located.

The association also supports children affected by the disappearances. Kashim said it was assisting about 600 orphaned children from affected families. Some attend school while others have dropped out because their relatives cannot afford to pay for their education or other basic needs.

“We are now suffering because of the harsh living conditions,” he said, adding that the ICRC had distributed relief items to some families.

When a missing person is a parent or breadwinner, relatives must cope with lost income while trying to provide food, shelter and schooling for children. news.originalContent:
Cypriots say Israeli money is moving fast and shutting them out as their government embraces Israel as a key ally.

Various locations, Cyprus – This summer in Cyprus, on a road near Larnaca airport, a billboard greeted holidaymakers in Hebrew: “Israelis, enjoy! Now come back and win!”

It was an election poster in the Cypriot city for Israel’s October 27 vote featuring Israel’s former army chief and leader of the opposition Yashar Party, Gadi Eisenkot.

The poster of Eisenkot, believed to be the first time a foreign politician had campaigned on billboards in Cyprus, signalled the growing number of Israelis living on and visiting the island, TV presenter and pro-Palestine activist Melanie Steliou told Al Jazeera.

“Israel is only 40 minutes away by plane; they can pop over, vote, and come back within the day,” she said.

Israel does not allow most citizens living abroad to vote outside the country, so campaigns court those who can fly home on polling day.

The poster demonstrates how Israeli politicians see Cyprus as “just another district of Israel”, Steliou said.

Israeli political influence is also being felt in Cyprus’s parliament. On October 20, six Cypriot lawmakers formed a pro-Israel caucus, launched by the advocacy group Israel Allies Foundation, The Jerusalem Post reported.

Cyprus has absorbed waves of foreign buyers before. Limassol was once nicknamed “Limassolgrad” for its Russian community.

Theodosis Pipis, a Cypriot historian and analyst with the think tank KEDISA, said that with Russian investment in the early 2010s, “you saw big buildings pop up” as companies moved over but “you never really saw a huge influx of buying houses, building schools, creating communities.”

Waves of foreign money before had not shaped the island’s political climate or brought foreign election campaigns with it, he said. Israeli investment, by contrast, is creating “a sense of community for the future”, he explained.

Israelis made nearly 600,000 trips to Cyprus last year, more than double the 2022 figure, according to the Cyprus Statistical Service (CYSTAT). In August, nearly one in four tourists arriving on the island was Israeli, a 28.4 percent increase from 2025, according to CYSTAT, with some buying homes.

In the 12 months to September 2025, Israelis made 850 property purchases in Larnaca district, more than any other foreign nationality, according to Ministry of Interior data. Israel’s embassy in Nicosia estimates that 15,000 to 20,000 consider the island home, Cypriot news outlet Philenews reported in August. According to the last census in 2021, slightly more than 1,000 Israelis lived in or were registered in Cyprus.

Venetians, Ottomans and the British all held the island before independence in 1960. It has been divided since Turkiye’s 1974 invasion, which followed a coup backed by the military government in Athens.

More recently, British retirees, Russian capital and golden-passport buyers have poured money into its property market.

But the speed, scale and nature of new Israeli investments, to an island where walls are covered in pro-Palestine murals and graffiti amid the genocide in Gaza, have caught the attention of many.

Investment from Israel rose more than sixfold between 2017 and 2024, to 5.1 billion euros ($5.9bn), according to the Central Bank of Cyprus, even as total foreign investment in the country fell by a quarter between 2022 and 2024 and Russian holdings, much of it money simply routed through Cypriot holding companies, shrank by more than a third.

Nasia Hadjigeorgiou, an associate professor in transitional justice and human rights at the University of Central Lancashire in Cyprus, told Al Jazeera that British and Lebanese buying “wasn’t something that made waves” and “came almost naturally”. The Israeli push, by contrast, “was a more sudden development”.

That timing matters, Hadjigeorgiou said. Israel’s government keeps receiving “a lot of cover and a lot of support” from Nicosia at a time when Israel “is doing unspeakable things” in the Palestinian enclave, “and that makes at least a portion of the population uncomfortable.”

Steliou pulled out her phone and showed one video – footage of a person who had been dining at an Israeli-owned restaurant attempting to attack protesters at a pro-Palestine march in Cyprus. Then another – an Israeli man writing expletives, drawing a sexual organ and spitting on a mural honouring Gaza’s children.

Such events occur often, she said.

Amid Israel’s wars on Gaza and Lebanon, locals interviewed by Al Jazeera said the presence of Israelis who had served in the military was hard to bear.

“I feel my heart sink when I hear and see large groups of Israeli men here, knowing that they have served in the military and can commit genocide and then buy property,” Giorgos Kyrou, a 32-year-old artist from Limassol, said.

Others blamed the government.

“Our politicians are compromised,” said Ioannis Nestoras, a potter who lives in Limassol. “They are willing to hug, to embrace, to treat as friends the Israeli government … I don’t think it’s representative of the Cypriot mentality.”

Outside the NYX Hotel Limassol, owned by Fattal, Israel’s largest hotel group, Steliou said Israeli investment appears centred on residential zones, including so-called “gated communities”.

Politicians, estate agents, academics and residents in Cyprus use the phrase to describe clusters of Israeli-owned properties they see as closed off from the wider community.

No official count exists, and owners’ nationalities are not recorded for purchases through Cypriot companies.

But patterns are visible. Israeli companies have bought most of the coastline between Livadia and Pyla, near Larnaca, to build homes and hotels, the Cypriot financial news site Stockwatch reported last year.

Stockwatch also reported that Israeli investors are promoting the largest organised residential development in Cyprus in Dromolaxia-Meneou, near Larnaca, with its own kindergarten, swimming pools, and private park.

Other Cypriots share Steliou’s concerns.

Kyrou said Israeli investments can focus on a particular area and that “sometimes it feels like the locals are being pushed out of those villages or urban centres”.

As a historian, Pipis said he understood fears that Israel’s occupation of Palestine could be repeated, though he did not expect that in Cyprus. Instead, he believes a foothold in a friendly EU member state “offers a certain safety if things escalate more in the Middle East”.

“You don’t buy these amounts of land preparing to create communities with schools … if you’re not planning to stay there for the long term,” he said.

In Polemidia, on the edge of Limassol, the Yael Foundation is funding a “flagship Jewish school” for up to 1,500 pupils, due to open in 2027. Cyprus has many private and international schools serving foreign communities.

Rabbi Yehoshua Smukler, who leads the project, has described this one as a “Zionist school”.

Critics also point to a pattern of building first and seeking permission later.

In February 2025, Cyprus’s Ministry of Education said that no application had been submitted for the school, and as late as October that year, the Ministry of Finance said the application was still being finalised, the Cypriot daily Kathimerini reported. Polemidia’s municipality, which complained it was not consulted, had itself been refused permission to build a sport centre on the same plot, the newspaper said.

The ministry did not respond to Al Jazeera’s questions.

In addition to schools, other infrastructure catering to Israelis has popped up.

Hadassah, one of the biggest hospital groups in Israel, owned by the US group “Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America”, opened its first European medical centre in Limassol in July.

“Specific areas are being bought en masse”, Stefanos Stefanou, leader of the left-wing Cypriot AKEL Party, said in June 2025. Purchases in Larnaca and Limassol were creating gated communities “almost inaccessible to anyone other than Israeli nationals”, he said, adding that Israel is preparing a “backyard” in Cyprus.

“We do not say this because of xenophobia or anti-Semitism,” he later said.

Israel’s former Ambassador to Cyprus Oren Anolik hit back, saying Stefanou’s comments sought to “single out the Jewish community in Cyprus”.

Hadjigeorgiou said there was likely “some exaggeration in relation to some of the examples” of closed-off areas, but that some were “very clearly gated communities”.

Speaking as a lawyer, she said Cyprus’s constitution and the European Convention on Human Rights prohibit discrimination on grounds including ethnicity, nationality and religion and that a development where only Israelis can buy “is unconstitutional”.

In western Cyprus, Uriel Kertesz, a businessman with Hungarian and Israeli citizenship, bought an estimated 70 to 80 percent of the abandoned village of Trozena and its surrounding farmland, which lies in a protected area. Yiannis Pazouros, a journalist at the Cypriot daily Politis who investigated the purchases and met Kertesz, said buying as an EU citizen freed him from limits on non-EU buyers.

Kertesz paid double or triple the market value and pushed ahead without the permits needed in a protected area, Pazouros said. Al Jazeera cannot independently confirm this.

Despite public fears that the village could be closed off, Kertesz has stayed tight-lipped about his plans, he added.

Criticism of Israel is far from uncommon in Cyprus, particularly in light of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Recently, on an October evening, Mike Kroll, an Israeli-American comedian based in Tel Aviv, played at a comedy festival in Limassol.

It initially caused “apprehension” because of Israel’s image, he said.

He felt “fine” with people criticising Israel because he was treated with respect and had engaged in “deep discussions”.

However, his reaction has not been not universal.

Across Cyprus, pro-Palestinian slogans turn public spaces into expressions of solidarity. Some are more direct in their meaning: “Zionists not welcome” reads graffiti in Larnaca.

In August 2025, after Israel’s Diaspora Affairs Minister Amichai Chikli complained to Cypriot ministers, the Interior Ministry ordered municipalities to remove what it called hate-inciting graffiti.

In Limassol, crews removed it with uncharacteristic efficiency, sometimes before 6am, Nestoras said. The mayor initially tried to protect it as political expression but was overruled, fuelling suspicion the order came from “higher-ups”.

The Interior Ministry did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

For Cypriots, Hadjigeorgiou said, the changes carry particular weight.

“We are a population that has been displaced from our homes in what the government loudly and clearly describes as ethnic cleansing. And at the same time, we are allowing another group to do the same thing in the areas that the Republic of Cyprus controls.”

news.originalContent:
Netanyahu and his rivals are tied days from the vote, and both camps are fighting with bots, deepfakes and data.

Polls show the blocs linked to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the opposition, led by former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, are locked in a virtual tie before Tuesday’s general election.

Efforts to mobilise supporters, win voters and attack opponents are being played out online through a series of social media advertisements and doctored AI videos. Many of these paint a bleak vision, the outcome depending on whether the party is on the right or centre, of Israel if their rivals win.

On Thursday, the Israeli liberal daily Haaretz reported that dozens of online bots created to undermine the Iranian government were being repurposed to spread campaign propaganda supporting Netanyahu and his Likud party, and warn voters of the dangers posed by Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who make up part of the opposition bloc.

Both camps are pushing AI-generated and deepfake videos on X. Several of them show Netanyahu confronting his alleged failings before the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023; others show the opposition being sympathetic to Arab parties (those representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel) which have been perceived by many as kingmakers in the coming election.

“We’re competing against parties with far greater budgets and technological resources, particularly the Likud,” Mauricio Lapchik, director of the Arab-dominated Joint List Hebrew-language campaign, said. “The use of technology is clearly deepening an already unequal playing field … We may not have the same resources, but we are convinced that our message matters more than the artificial technology behind it.”

Significant resources have been used by the Israeli right against the left-wing Joint List – an alliance of Hadash, Balad and Ta’al – and Ra’am, also known as the United Arab List. Palestinian citizens of Israel generally support one of these two blocs, and all the parties have faced legal challenges before the parliamentary election.

Likud were looking to use Elector, an app that tracks voter turnout on election day, but were restricted by the Central Elections Committee due to privacy concerns. They will instead use a new app named Victory 26. Unlike Elector, this does not reveal the identities of voters but would allow Likud activists and officials to determine which areas have the lowest turnout, manually take the names of people who have cast their votes, and then target those who have not yet.

Likud is encouraging supporters and potential sympathisers to download and use the app on election day, according to Haaretz.

This app could play a crucial role in the election, which will likely be determined by voter turnout.

“Elector and similar programmes are very basic compared to what the Israeli military is capable of now,” Sebastian Ben Daniel, a doctoral researcher into algorithms, computability, and AI, said. “Israel has the perfect laboratory with which to develop this kind of technology.”

Privacy issues are a particular concern for the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population and whose political activity is already heavily monitored.

A woman was sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park Saturday night, according to the NYPD.

A brazen man approached a woman while brandishing a knife before sexually assaulting her inside the park near East 67th Street and Fifth Avenue around 8:30 p.m., cops said.

The woman was rushed to an area hospital where she is listed in stable condition.

The armed thug fled the scene wearing a black sweatshirt and pants with a black backpack, cops said.

Further information was not immediately available Saturday night.

Nearby residents were left shaken after hearing about the heinous assault.

“It’s very concerning for a very great area of New York City, and I’m uneasy with my fiancé walking her dog at night,” local resident Davis Defore told The Post.

Defore, 30, said he was just in Central Park walking his dog Harlow before the scene unfolded.

“I was like, ‘Oh, my goodness.’ It’s literally that same path. I let Harlow out in the field right there to go play,” he recalled.

Another local, 30-year-old Valentina Mizrahi, has lived in the neighborhood since 2021 and said she’s never been scared but her mother recently warned her not to walk alone at night “because it gets ugly” after having a conversation with a nearby hotel doorman.

No arrests have been made as of Saturday night.

news.originalContent:
Polls show populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in a tight race against the anticorruption and anti-authoritarian movement.

Serbians are voting in parliamentary elections amid a mass student protest ⁠movement that seeks to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has held power as prime minister and then president for more than a decade.

The snap elections, called by Vucic in September, follow almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption ⁠and creeping authoritarianism, triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.

The students have since gained widespread support.

A loss for Vucic ⁠would mark a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary’s Viktor Orban in April.

But Vucic, who resigned as president in September to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia out of economic obscurity and ‌orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation.

“The Serbian election ⁠is shaping up to be a watershed moment for the country as the Student List mounts the biggest challenge against Vucic yet,” Mario Bikarski, senior Europe analyst at risk consultancy Verisk Maplecroft, told the Reuters news agency.

During the campaign, Vucic has promised higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare, and subsidies for young couples. He has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union.

But relations with the EU have frayed under his leadership, with the bloc growing increasingly frustrated over a lack of reforms addressing the judiciary, the rule of law and corruption.

The Student List movement’s agenda focuses on rooting out corruption and improving schooling, while saying little about their international ambitions.

Their roster of 250 largely unfamiliar candidates, including university professors, actors and farmers, is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.

Opinion polls are predicting a tight race.

An Ipsos poll published on Thursday gives Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party 47 percent ⁠of the vote to the students’ 40 percent, though other polls have put the students ahead.

Rights groups and activists say repression has worsened since the deadly train station canopy collapse, which was widely blamed on government corruption and sparked the student demonstrations.

About 150,000 supporters of the student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday.

Vucic and his party have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents.

The former president claims the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students deny.

MILWAUKEE — Sal Frelick tied the score with his first home run in three months, Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead single in the seventh inning and the Milwaukee Brewers stunned the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 on Saturday night for a 2-0 World Series lead by overcoming a four-run deficit for the second time this postseason.

Tampa Bay, which won the AL pennant in part by consistently forcing opponents into mistakes, committed one error, made two other misplays on defense and had a runner thrown out at the plate by Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio.u

Down 4-0 in the first inning, Milwaukee rallied for its seventh comeback win of this postseason. The Brewers also rebounded from a 4-0 deficit to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NL Championship Series, completing a four-game sweep.

“As long as there’s game left, we have a chance. I think we’ve all bought into that. We’re never out of it,” Pratt said.

After losing Friday’s opener 3-2, the Rays burst ahead against rookie Logan Henderson but the Brewers started to claw back with two runs in the bottom half off Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen.

David Hamilton cut the deficit to 4-3 with a run-scoring grounder in the fourth and Frelick capped a nine-pitch at-bat against Ian Seymour in the sixth by driving a fastball over the center-field fence.

Frelick had gone 103 plate appearances without a home run since his July 11 drive off Pittsburgh’s Braxton Ashcraft and had not gone deep against a lefty pitcher since opening day against Tyler Gilbert of the Chicago White Sox. Frelick sped around the bases in 18.72 seconds, half the time of some theatrical trots this postseason.

“I was just pumped to try to get back to the dugout,” the 5-foot-9 Frelick said. “I don’t hit a lot of home runs, especially to center, so I was happy it went out.”

Screaming fans at Milwaukee’s first World Series since 1982 were fired up during the seventh-inning stretch, dancing to the “Beer Barrel Polka” played by Mike Schneider, an accordionist from Clinton, Wisconsin.

“It’s mayhem, and I’ve never experienced anything like it before,” Frelick said. “It’s been motivating for all the players.”

Brice Turang doubled against losing pitcher Tyler Wells on the second pitch of the bottom half, advanced on Garrett Mitchell’s deep flyout to right and scored when Pratt, a 22-year-old shortstop who debuted in June, looped a sinker from Kevin Kelly into short right field.

“I feel like we’ve been down a lot early throughout the playoffs so far,” Frelick said. “Nine innings to play, and it doesn’t really change your offensive plan at all. We’re trying to go up, take a chunk of the pitcher each at-bat, pass it to the next guy and hopefully that leads to a few runs doing that.”

Abner Uribe pitched 1 1/3 hitless innings for the win.

Jonny DeLuca doubled off Aaron Ashby starting the ninth, then Victor Mesa Jr. struck out when he couldn’t check his swing. Pinch-hitter Ben Williamson’s groundout advanced the runner and Yandy Díaz struck out when he couldn’t check his swing on a full-count pitch.

Ashby has three saves in the postseason while not allowing a run.

“Look, we didn’t play our cleanest baseball game by any stretch,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “We pride ourselves on doing everything we can to support the pitchers and making plays behind them. Today was probably not our best day.”

Milwaukee won its seventh straight game, becoming the fifth team to twice overcome four-run deficits for victories in a single postseason and the first since Philadelphia in 2022.

Game 3 of the matchup between teams seeking their first title is Monday night at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida, where the Brewers last played in 2023.

Of the 57 previous teams to take 2-0 World Series leads, 46 claimed the championship.

Tampa Bay took a 4-2 lead in the highest-scoring Series first inning since 1993’s Game 4 as the teams combined for seven hits, tying the most in an opening frame.

Henderson followed Jacob Misiorowski in the Brewers’ rotation, the first time teammates 24 or younger started the first two games of a World Series since Cincinnati’s Gary Nolan and Ross Grimsley in 1972.

Henderson started on 11 days’ rest and struggled as the Rays fouled off 13 of 35 pitches in the first. He gave up four runs — three earned — in three innings.

Given an extra day of rest, Rasmussen allowed three runs and six hits over 3 2/3 innings in his shortest start since July 9.

“Just felt like he wasn’t as sharp as he’s been for quite some time,” Cash said.

Pratt made his fourth error of the postseason, the Brewers’ ninth in 10 games, bouncing his throw past first baseman Jake Bauers on a leadoff grounder by Díaz. Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero followed with RBI singles, and Liam Hicks hit a two-run homer.

Chourio and Bauers started the bottom half with singles and first baseman Jonathan Aranda allowed Contreras’ one-out foul pop to bounce out of his mitt near netting in front of the seats.

With Bauers running on a full-count pitch, Contreras bounced an RBI single to the left of second baseman Richie Palacios, who had taken a step toward the bag. Mitchell’s two-out single cut the deficit to 4-2.

Hamilton hit an RBI grounder in the fourth that bounced under Aranda’s legs for an error.

Chourio threw out Hicks for the final out of the sixth when third base coach Brady Williams waved the slow-footed catcher to try to score from second on Mesa’s single.

“I think we’ve made some mistakes on the bases for sure, going back to yesterday,” Cash said. “To their credit, they have responded with everything that we have thrown at them in these first two games.”

Although not pretty, No. 17 Texas was able to get the job done on Saturday night in Austin, Texas.

Despite a second-half comeback attempt by No. 7-ranked Mississippi, the Longhorns were able to stave off the Rebels in a gritty 34-27 win.

The game proved crucial for quarterback Arch Manning, whose shaky junior season put his starting job in jeopardy, with backup KJ Lacey receiving more reps with the first-team offense this week.

Ahead of Saturday, Manning had thrown for just 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions.

Under the pressure, Texas’ offense jumped out to a hot start on Saturday, scoring 21 unanswered points to the tune of a 24-3 lead headed into halftime.

During that first-half surge, Manning threw a 50-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo in the second quarter. He should have had a 59-yarder to Cam Coleman, who dropped an easy catch on a deep throw in the first quarter before exiting with what appeared to be a shoulder injury on the first play of the second half.

Despite Texas’ quick start, Ole Miss wasted no time coming back in the second half, scoring two touchdowns in the third to put the game within a possession.

Then to open up the fourth, Rebels QB Trinidad Chambliss (25-for-52 for 250 yards and two touchdowns plus three interceptions) found wideout Horatio Fields for a 27-yard touchdown to tie the game at 24.

Manning — who went 18-for-30 for 212 yards with a touchdown, two interceptions and one fumble — threw a pick on the next drive, but the Texas defense was able to finally stop the Rebels to keep the game tied.

Texas then reclaimed the lead thanks to a rushing touchdown from Manning, his second of the night.

After a missed field goal from Ole Miss, the Longhorns kicked a 33-yarder to put them up two scores.

news.originalContent:
The settlement is the second-largest after an $880m ​deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los ​Angeles in 2024.

The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay more than $800m to settle the legal claims of about 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy.

New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks said on Saturday that the settlement will be formally signed on November 6 after an agreement with the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote in an email sent to his priests and shared by the archdiocese’s news outlet.

“This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” he added.

According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 survivors will receive at least $250,000 from the Archdiocese of New York and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.

The settlement is the second-largest of its kind after an $880m deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.

“The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, a lawyer representing people who filed more than 1,000 claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement.

“Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.”

The agreement marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the Catholic Church in the United States has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.

In the 2000s, media investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the US had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.

Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programmes have been created to compensate survivors without going to trial.

In June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395m to about 530 survivors of sexual abuse committed by its clergy to settle their lawsuits.

news.originalContent:
Barcelona vs Real Madrid will see the return of Spanish football’s fiercest rivalry between two star-studded teams.

Barcelona, Spain – It has been 15 years since Jose Mourinho was first thrown into the ring of fire at Camp Nou and the famously polarising manager’s Real Madrid side was handed a La Liga battering by Barcelona.

The home team’s supporters have not forgotten that cold November night from 2010, when Pep Guardiola’s men stamped their authority with a 5-0 win.

It became an enduring image of a rivalry that spilled from the pitch onto the touchline, sparking heated confrontations among players and bitter exchanges between managers for years to come.

Now, Barcelona – the city and the club – are ready to “welcome back” Mourinho on his second stint as the manager of their fiercest rival.

“I remember the 5-0 [scoreline] but also the tension,” recalls Aleix Soler, a Barcelona fan.

“You’d spend the whole week arguing about the game even before a ball was kicked,” he tells Al Jazeera at a Barcelona fan zone.

The 35-year-old culer – as Barcelona’s supporters are known – will watch the match, having also attended games during Mourinho’s first Madrid spell.

“Beating Madrid is always special, but against Mourinho, you’re still smiling on Monday morning.”

As Mourinho returns to the fixture after 13 years on Sunday, he will face another Barcelona side that has set a punishing pace in the league.

The spotlight will be on Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe – with their growing rivalry adding another dramatic layer to the plot.

The two forwards meet a day before the Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London, bringing individual ambition to a contest that isn’t shorn of consequences for either club.

Barcelona have won all nine of their league games, scoring 39 goals, and lead Madrid by six points.

Victory would stretch that gap to nine. A Madrid win would not only reduce it to three points, but also inject new belief in Mourinho’s side.

Mourinho acknowledged the significance of the occasion after his team’s Champions League victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

“It’s another league match, but it’s not a match like the others,” he told local broadcaster Movistar.

Madrid are third in La Liga standings, behind Atletico Madrid, and have lost six of their past seven Clasicos. Mourinho must find a way to interrupt that pattern before the title chase intensifies.

While Hansi Flick has made this fixture a source of strength for Barcelona in his two years as manager, the hosts approach it with their own questions after a 4-2 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, their first loss of the season, on Tuesday.

Barcelona scored freely against Getafe, Galatasaray and Real Betis before travelling to France. In Paris, their attacking threat remained but defensive absences and the spaces opened up to PSG made the evening uncomfortable.

Barcelona defenders Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde were out injured, leaving Flick with Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo as full-back options on either side of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin.

Kounde remained absent from training on Friday, while midfielder Dani Olmo’s adductor injury further narrowed the coach’s options.

Madrid enjoyed a more encouraging European evening, beating Leipzig 4-1 with goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Mbappe and Yan Diomande.

Their three wins from three Champions League games offer a foundation, even if domestic consistency has proved harder to establish.

However, they will face Barcelona without the suspended Vinicius Junior, removing one of their most dangerous runners and leaving Mourinho with another decision to make about Mbappe.

Yan Diomande offers an alternative on the left, while Guler’s passing and Jude Bellingham’s movement could be essential to getting Madrid’s leading scorer into dangerous positions.

The task begins with escaping Barcelona’s pressure. If Madrid can move the ball beyond the first challenge and find a passer facing forward, Mbappe can attack the space behind Flick’s defensive line.

For Barcelona, maintaining pressure on that passer will be as important as tracking the run. Retreat too readily, and they risk losing the compact shape that allows them to recover possession and keep attacks coming.

Federico Valverde’s recent deployment at right-back gives Madrid another route forward, with his overlapping runs complementing teammates who move inside.

Whether Mourinho keeps him there will help determine the balance between creativity and defensive cover in midfield.

Madrid must decide how much attention they can afford to give Yamal.

The young sensation’s dribbling can draw a second defender towards Barcelona’s right wing, but that help comes at a cost elsewhere as Pedri can redirect possession towards the space left open.

Meanwhile, Raphinha’s movement threatens opponents concentrating on the ball, and his 12 league goals underline the danger of treating Barcelona as a one-man attack.

Stopping Yamal from beating his marker will achieve little success if the supporting defensive movements leave another player free.

For Real Madrid fans, one glorious night at Camp Nou could be seen as a turning point.

“Winning there would make me believe we can win the league, especially if we play with courage”, says Lucia Martin, a Madrid supporter.

The 26-year-old is travelling to Barcelona with her father to attend the game, and much of her hope rests on Mbappe, although she wants the team to share the responsibility.

“When he gets the ball, I always think something can happen, but we can’t spend 90 minutes waiting for him to rescue us.”

Despite leading all conversations around the match, Yamal and Mbappe will rarely confront each other directly; their influence will be measured in the problems they create for everyone else.

Yamal has eight goals and six assists in nine league appearances. Mbappe has nine goals and two assists across the same number of games.

One can pull defenders towards the ball before releasing a teammate, the other can force them backwards with the threat of a run.

Both are nominees for the upcoming Ballon d’Or and although the match falls outside the assessment period for this year’s award, it will serve as the perfect build-up to one of the most hotly-contested awards in recent years.

Before football celebrates its outstanding performers in London, two of its strongest claimants to the title of world’s best will share a stage where reputations are tested under exceptional pressure and strengthen their claim as the world’s best.

On the eve of the Ballon d’Or, Yamal has a chance to extend Barcelona’s perfect start and deepen Madrid’s frustration.

For Mbappe, there is the opportunity to bring his team back into the race at their rival’s expense.

news.title: تظاهرات هزاران نفر علیه نتانیاهو در تل‌آویو، سه روز مانده به انتخابات اسرائیل
news.originalSummary:
هزاران نفر روز شنبه ۲۴ اکتبر، سه روز  به انتخابات مجلس اسرائیل، در تل‌آویو علیه دولت بنیامین نتانیاهو تظاهرات کردند. این انتخابات در حالی برگزار می‌شود که سه سال جنگ در غزه و درگیری‌های نظامی با لبنان و ایران، همراه با نگرانی از انزوای بین‌المللی و پیامدهای اقتصادی آن، به محورهای اصلی رقابت‌های سیاسی اسرائیل تبدیل شده‌اند.

news.originalContent:
هزاران نفر روز شنبه ۲۴ اکتبر، سه روز  به انتخابات مجلس اسرائیل، در تل‌آویو علیه دولت بنیامین نتانیاهو تظاهرات کردند. این انتخابات در حالی برگزار می‌شود که سه سال جنگ در غزه و درگیری‌های نظامی با لبنان و ایران، همراه با نگرانی از انزوای بین‌المللی و پیامدهای اقتصادی آن، به محورهای اصلی رقابت‌های سیاسی اسرائیل تبدیل شده‌اند.

به گزارش خبرگزاری فرانسه، رهبران چهار حزب اصلی مخالف دولت، از جمله گادی آیزنکوت، رئیس پیشین ستاد ارتش اسرائیل و مهم‌ترین رقیب انتخاباتی نتانیاهو، در تجمع روز شنبه شرکت کردند.

این تظاهرات را گروهی به نام «شورای اکتبر» سازمان‌دهی کرد که خانواده‌های قربانیان و گروگان‌های حمله هفتم اکتبر ۲۰۲۳ حماس آن را تشکیل داده‌اند.

این گروه خواستار تشکیل کمیسیون مستقل دولتی برای بررسی ناکامی‌های امنیتی منجر به حمله حماس و مشخص شدن مسئولیت مقام‌های اسرائیل است.

شرکت‌کنندگان در این تجمع از میدان رابین به طرف میدان گروگان‌ها در تل‌آویو راهپیمایی کردند؛ مکانی که در سال‌های گذشته از مراکز اصلی تجمع‌های اعتراضی علیه دولت نتانیاهو بوده است.

به گزارش رسانه‌های اسرائیلی، گادی آیزنکوت هنگام ورود به محل تجمع با استقبال گرم معترضان روبه‌رو شد.

هاداس فویراشتاین، ۶۸ ساله و از شرکت‌کنندگان این تظاهرات، به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت: «عملکرد کسانی که در چهار سال گذشته کشور ما را رهبری کرده‌اند، بسیار بود‌. اسرائیل هیچ‌وقت در چنین وضعیتی نبوده است.»

دولت نتانیاهو با تشکیل کمیسیون مستقل دولتی برای بررسی ناکامی‌های امنیتی هفتم اکتبر مخالفت کرده و به‌جای آن پیشنهاد تشکیل کمیسیونی را داده است که نیمی از اعضای آن را ائتلاف حاکم و نیم دیگر را نمایندگان مخالف دولت تعیین کنند.

رهبران احزاب مخالف گفته‌اند که چنین کمیسیونی را تحریم خواهند کرد.

انتخابات پارلمانی اسرائیل روز سه‌شنبه ۲۷ اکتبر برگزار می‌شود. تازه‌ترین نظرسنجی‌ها از رقابت نزدیک اردوگاه حامی نتانیاهو با احزاب مخالف او حکایت دارند.

بر اساس نظرسنجی شبکه کان، رسانه عمومی اسرائیل، احزاب مخالف نتانیاهو ممکن است ۵۲ کرسی و ائتلاف حامی او ۵۰ کرسی از مجموع ۱۲۰ کرسی پارلمان را به دست آورند.

۱۸ کرسی باقی‌مانده نیز به احزابی تعلق می‌گیرد که در هیچ‌یک از این دو اردوگاه قرار ندارند؛ از جمله احزاب عرب.

از آنجا که تشکیل دولت در اسرائیل به حمایت دست‌کم ۶۱ نماینده نیاز دارد، نتایج این نظرسنجی نشان می‌دهد که هیچ‌یک از دو اردوگاه به‌تنهایی از اکثریت لازم برخوردار نیست.

تازه‌ترین نظرسنجی‌ها پیش از آغاز ممنوعیت انتشار نظرسنجی‌های انتخاباتی در شامگاه جمعه منتشر شد.

یکی دیگر از موضوعاتی که در روزهای پایانی کارزار انتخاباتی اسرائیل به بحثی جنجالی تبدیل شده، نگرانی از انزوای اقتصادی آن کشور است.

بریتانیا و شماری از کشورهای دیگر در واکنش به افزایش حملات شهرک‌نشینان اسرائیلی به فلسطینی‌ها در کرانه باختری اشغالی و گسترش شهرک‌سازی، تحریم‌هایی را علیه کالاهای تولیدشده در شهرک‌های اسرائیلی وضع کرده‌اند.

بنیامین نتانیاهو روز جمعه گفت که اسرائیل ممکن است برای مقابله با پیامدهای انزوای بین‌المللی، به ایجاد سازوکارهای جایگزین در اقتصاد دیجیتال، از جمله استفاده از رمزارزها، نیاز داشته باشد.

او همچنین هشدار داد که بسته‌های تسلیحاتی چندمیلیارددلاری آمریکا برای اسرائیل ممکن است در آینده همچون گذشته ادامه پیدا نکند.

این اظهارات با واکنش تند رهبران مخالف دولت روبه‌رو شد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

گادی آیزنکوت، رئیس پیشین ستاد ارتش اسرائیل و رقیب اصلی بنیامین نتانیاهو در انتخابات پیش رو، در شبکه ایکس با کنایه به پیشنهاد نخست‌وزیر از اصطلاح «بی‌بی‌کوین» استفاده کرد؛ ترکیبی از لقب شناخته‌شده نتانیاهو، «بی‌بی»، و واژه «کوین» به معنای سکه که در نام بسیاری از رمزارزها به کار می‌رود.

آیزنکوت نوشت که نتانیاهو در صورت پیروزی دوباره، اسرائیل را از اقتصاد جهانی جدا خواهد کرد و این وضعیت به خرید اینترنتی، سرمایه‌گذاری در صنایع پیشرفته و امنیت کشور آسیب خواهد زد.

او هشدار داد که نباید اجازه داد طرحی که آن را «بی‌بی‌کوین» نامیده، اقتصاد اسرائیل را نابود کند.

یائیر لاپید، نخست‌وزیر پیشین و رهبر کنونی مخالفان، نیز نتانیاهو را متهم کرد که چشم‌اندازی از کمبود کالا و مشکلات اقتصادی پیش روی شهروندان قرار می‌دهد.

لاپید در مصاحبه با شبکه ۱۲ اسرائیل گفت که ادامه نخست‌وزیری نتانیاهو ممکن است به تحریم‌های بیشتر، از دست رفتن توافق‌های امنیتی با آمریکا و آسیب شدید به اقتصاد اسرائیل منجر شود.

بانک مرکزی اسرائیل نیز اعلام کرد که رمزارزها راهکاری برای دور زدن تحریم‌های بین‌المللی نیستند و تأکید کرد که حفظ روابط اقتصادی با شرکای تجاری اصلی باید در اولویت قرار گیرد.

Three men from the Dominican Republic are begging to be rescued from Russia, where they claimed they were lured by false promises of jobs — and then sent to the battlefield in the war with Ukraine.

In a video posted on social media last week, the three unnamed men alleged they were conscripted in the Russian military and sent to the front lines of the four-year-old war.

“We were deceived, contrary to what is being said, that we came here knowing what we were getting into,” one of the soldiers said. “That’s a lie. We were brought here under an employment contract – to work.”

Dominican nationals are required by law to seek permission from the government if they wish to join another country’s armed forces and could lose their citizenship if they do so without approval.

The Dominican men did not reveal when they first arrived or how long they have been in Russia; what, if any, training they had received; how they were recruited, or how much they were paid. They also didn’t share what jobs they thought they would be doing in Russia.

One of the soldiers described the grim reality of life on the battlefield, alleging the Russians have treated them as “slaves” as they face drone attacks by Ukrainian forces.

“When those people send us to the front, there are drones that show no mercy to anyone,” he said. “When one of them crashes into you – boom! It blows you to bits, shredding you into tiny, bite-sized pieces.”

The Dominican men claimed that on average, only two out every 100 soldiers survive their missions.

One of the soldiers said in the video that fighters from Perú, Panamá and India already were pulled out from Russia and repatriated to their home countries.

Panama’s Foreign Relations Ministry was able to arrange the return of 17 Panamanians, including 11 who fought on the Russian side, while Peru has managed the return of 50 of it citizens, including four young men who escaped a Russian training center. The Indian government has ensured the release of 139 nationals who went to Russia to join the army.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

California is on the brink — of taking a simple step toward election security.

The feds have been handing down scrutiny to make sure some murky elements from California’s election process are sorted out and exposed before the polls close on Nov. 3.

It’s all coming at a time of golden opportunity to help secure the Golden State’s elections, with Proposition 39, the voter ID measure, hanging in the balance — a measure that California voters can put over the line.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

The stakes are high. Last week, the Department of Justice filed an emergency order to prevent California election officials from immediately counting ballots tied to 20,000 suspected noncitizen voters.

After California Attorney General Rob Bonta moved to dismiss the DOJ’s lawsuit, the Department of Justice appealed to the 9th Circuit, which set a hearing set for Sunday, Oct. 25.

The DOJ’s efforts are timely, and welcome — but while the feds act from on high, you, the California voter, have the chance to secure California’s elections by voting for Prop. 39 on Election Day.

And the need for such security is enormous, as Bill Essayli, LA’s top federal prosecutor, has shown.

On Oct. 19, Essayli announced the arrest of 28 noncitizens who allegedly registered to vote in California elections, some of whom allegedly voted in multiple elections. Of that number, 12 were registered in LA County.

The feds called it the largest voter fraud bust in California history.

And if the 20,000 number — which Essayli called “the floor” — turns out to be to accurate, that would be an even more explosive revelation about how far our elections have fallen.

Though Democratic officials like Bonta hem and haw that voter fraud that does exist is a “drop in the bucket” that doesn’t affect electoral outcomes — that’s not true.

Every illegal vote undermines one of our nation’s most vaunted democratic principles — one citizen, one vote.

Of the 12 noncitizens from LA County arrested on Monday for allegedly illegally being registered to vote, one was a registered Democrat and two were registered Republicans (the rest were unaffiliated or registered with third parties).

As it turns out, election security is a bipartisan need that transcends the political spectrum.

A voter ID measure would help secure California’s elections and protect the franchise of the Golden State’s legitimate citizen voters.

Now’s the chance to make that happen.

Prop. 39 is a common-sense measure to help restore security and faith in California elections. It would require every voter to show identification in person, or, if voting by mail, to write the last four digits of an ID number on the ballot envelope.

It’s pretty simple. And given that you need an ID to purchase alcohol and cigarettes (as well as guns from federally licensed dealers), to drive a car or board a commercial flight, it makes perfect sense that you should produce a form of identification to vote.

It makes so much sense that Bonta has tried to confuse voters to torpedo the proposition’s chances. In July, he changed the measure’s title on the ballot to make it seem like the measure would disenfranchise legitimate voters.

But it would do no such thing.

Don’t let him fool you. And Prop. 39, despite his best efforts, just might pass.

The California Post’s new poll, conducted by McLaughlin & Associates, showed that support for Prop. 39 among California voters was evenly divided: 45.6% of voters said they would vote for the measure, and 47.8% said they would vote against it, with 5.9% undecided.

The dead heat reveals that with just a little more support, more-secure elections are achievable in California.

The only way to make sure it happens is to get out and vote yourself.

That may be the only way to ensure that your vote will matter in the future.

news.originalContent:
Gia Giudice defended her upscale new Westwood, New Jersey, eatery, Il Vero, after customers criticized the establishment for implementing a no-kids rule for its after-5 p.m. dining.

The “Real Housewives of New Jersey” personality, 25, took to TikTok to defend the decision after negative reviews populated online listings for the high profile restaurant — with a one-star Google review saying the establishment “probably won’t survive long” due to the policy.

“The first thing that I want to address is that we are a restaurant that only accommodates adult dining,” she said during a Get Ready With Me video on Sunday.

“While I know that might be a bummer to some who want to bring their kids out to dinner, there are many restaurants in Westwood that are kid-friendly,” she explained while applying makeup.

Westwood is a “family-oriented town,” Gia explained, “which is why we wanted to bring something a little different and bring a new atmosphere that adults were actually waiting for and the town of Westwood is loving.”

The restaurant — which states on its website is “intended for adult guests” and features Italian-Mediterranean dining — was created to make the experience “elevated,” Giudice said.

She also described Il Vero as a place that “makes you want to get dressed up” and go out.

The restaurant had been open for a week at the time of Giudice’s TikTok, but she claimed that they may eventually considering allowing children for lunch reservations only, which they are not yet accepting.

“Thank you for all the support,” Giudice captioned the video, adding a pink heart and promising that “this is only the beginning” for her restaurant.

The message came after a slew of online reviewers took the eatery to task for the no-kids policy.

Want more celebrity and pop culture news?

One person complained, “Some friends wanted to go with their kids and they said they could not try it because restaurant was kid free. How ridiculous.”

Another wrote, “No kids allowed. This surely won’t help this business. I give them 6 months.”

Others, however, were delighted by the rule, with one reviewer gushing, “Best part… No screaming children running around messing up my fancy dinner.”

Another wrote, “I love a restaurant that caters to adults and not children. Perfect date night!”

A third person labeled the eatery “grown and sexy.”

On TikTok, many of Giudice’s fans were equally supportive. “As a mom, I would LOVE a kids free restaurant for date night, girls night, etc.”

Another joked, “well my ‘kids’ are 26 and 28 and I’m still not bringing them!”

“Your restaurant your rules,” a third remarked. “Stay blessed.”

During an appearance of Page Six’s “Virtual Real-Tea” earlier this month, Giudice told co-hosts Evan Real and Danny Murphy that she’s “so happy” about the restaurant’s launch.

“We wanted to bring New York City vibes to New Jersey,” she explained of the restaurant’s luxurious, modern vibe.

The “Next Gen NYC” star also divulged she spends plenty of time there — which is a surprise for fans checking it out.

“I don’t think people are expecting me to be there as often as I am,” she laughed. “It’s fun because you’re watching your vision come to life.” She added, “They love to take photos with me.”

Reps for Il Vero and Giudice did not immediately respond to Page Six’s requests for comment on Saturday.

President Trump blasted Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff as a  “far-left extremist,” as he promised new jobs at a Georgia rally Saturday.

Trump ripped Ossoff for voting for policies he said brought about inflation and record-high illegal immigration during the Biden administration.

“Jon Ossoff is a far-left extremist that votes to destroy everything Georgia values,” Trump said as the crowd booed the Dem.

He also announced a new Audi plant in Macon, Georgia and said it would bring thousands of jobs to the state.

“Audi has just committed to invest 4.2 billion dollars in nearby Macon — to begin construction next month on a massive plant that will produce 200,000 cars per year,” he said to raucous cheers.

The president was in Perry, Georgia stumping for Rep. Mike Collins (R-Ga.) who is running to unseat Ossoff in the Senate, and for Rick Jackson who is running for governor against former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance-Bottoms.

Ossoff, who is widely thought of to be a leading contender for the Democratic nominee for president in 2028, is leading Collins by eight points, 48% to 40% with 12% undecided according to the latest AJC poll.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There was nothing but open field in front of the Michigan State defender after he picked up the fumble and raced past midfield with the score tied in the second quarter.

Chasing from the far side was an unlikely pursuer – UCLA’s quarterback.

As Ty Dieffenbach finally caught up to the Spartans’ Nikai Martinez around the Bruins’ 22-yard line Saturday afternoon, he made contact, holding Martinez up until his teammates could arrive to make the tackle.

Two plays later, Michigan State’s quarterback threw an interception leading to a UCLA touchdown. A game the Spartans could have been leading had Dieffenbach not displayed his speed and toughness – on defense, in essence – was now trending heavily in the Bruins’ direction.

Forget Dieffenbach’s huge touchdown pass in the third quarter.

This was the play of the game.

“Ty’s response at that moment of making sure he held that kid up until help showed up, it’s everything,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said after his ninth-ranked team overcame a horrible start to pull away for a 28-10 victory at the Rose Bowl. “It’s 14 points, right? I thought he did a great job.”

After shaking off a lower-body injury just before halftime, Dieffenbach returned to complete a 63-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Brian Rowe Jr. in the third quarter. Rowe made the play possible by badly beating his defender and reaching out to haul in the pass on his way to the end zone.

“Got a good play call, got the post against quarters, safety came down and we just launched it,” Dieffenbach said after improving to 2-0 as the Bruins’ starter for a team that remained unbeaten and in strong contention for the College Football Playoff. “It was a great catch and run and finish with the touchdown.”

For a few frightening moments late in the second quarter, it seemed as if Dieffenbach might be done for the day.

After getting crunched by a pack of defenders, he remained on the field for several minutes while trainers looked at him. Then he rose and walked slowly off the field.

With star quarterback Nico Iamaleava already having been lost for the season because of a knee injury suffered earlier this month, the Bruins (7-0 overall, 5-0 Big Ten) couldn’t afford to lose another quarterback.

But it soon became apparent that Dieffenbach would be back.

“It was just a cleat on like a weird spot where it was sensitive and felt nervy to him,” Chesney said of the situation, “but in the end, when he came in and moved around, he’s like, ‘I’m perfectly fine.’ ”

Dieffenbach lamented several passes he didn’t complete on the way to finishing 18 of 31 for 198 yards with 1 touchdown and no interceptions.

The senior didn’t need to be perfect on a day the Bruins rolled up 245 yards on the ground.

But the play that generated the most buzz afterward was Dieffenbach’s handiwork on defense.

“Ty’s fast,” UCLA defensive back Malik Hartford said after making his own huge contributions with a forced fumble and an interception. “Just appreciate him giving the defense a chance. I mean, that’s all you can ask for.”

Dieffenbach said his approach in that situation was to just get in front of Martinez and delay him long enough for someone to make the tackle.

“People don’t want to see their quarterback do that,” Dieffenbach said of trying to play defense and potentially getting hurt, “but for me, I’ll do whatever for this team – I’ll get in front of him, I’ll hit him if I have to. I tried to hit him but it’s been a while since I’ve made a tackle.”

He might as well have been credited with one, having symbolized his team’s resolve on a day that it needed it.

But the play that generated the most buzz afterward was Dieffenbach’s handiwork on defense.

“Ty’s fast,” UCLA defensive back Malik Hartford said after making his own huge contributions with a forced fumble and an interception. “Just appreciate him giving the defense a chance. I mean, that’s all you can ask for.”

Dieffenbach said his approach in that situation was to just get in front of Martinez and delay him long enough for someone to make the tackle.

“People don’t want to see their quarterback do that,” Dieffenbach said of trying to play defense and potentially getting hurt, “but for me, I’ll do whatever for this team – I’ll get in front of him, I’ll hit him if I have to. I tried to hit him but it’s been a while since I’ve made a tackle.”

He might as well have been credited with one, having symbolized his team’s resolve on a day that it needed it.

A high-profile Los Angeles immigration reporter has been fired amid allegations of ethical breaches, including claims he had a secret romantic relationship with a rising California state senator and allowed her to help write stories published under his byline.

Memo Torres, 46, abruptly parted ways with left-leaning news outlet L.A. TACO this week after an internal investigation that the publication says followed nearly five months of discussions over repeated violations of its policies and journalistic standards.

The split has sparked a public war of words between Torres and his former employer, with L.A. TACO pushing back against claims it forced him out to scale back its coverage of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids across Southern California.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“Memo Torres did important work here, and we’re grateful that he rose to the challenge when ICE began their siege of our city. But we fired him for repeated violations of our policies and our basic journalistic standards. That’s it. That’s the reason,” the outlet said in a statement published Saturday.

The publication said it gave Torres multiple opportunities to take responsibility and improve, insisting his departure had nothing to do with its immigration coverage.

“The rumor that we’ve turned our back on ICE coverage is a lie. And a dangerous one,” the statement said.

But according to reporting by LA Material, sources have raised questions about Torres’ coverage of Democratic state Sen. Sasha Renee Pérez, 34, including allegations that the pair had a personal relationship while he reported on her political agenda.

The most serious allegation is that Pérez was allowed to edit and write portions of stories published under Torres’ byline. The senator has strongly denied having any role in L.A. TACO’s editorial decisions.

“I did not write any articles or control the editorial decisions of L.A. Taco,” Pérez said in a statement. “Any person suggesting I wrote pieces for L.A. Taco is attempting to undermine my work and attack Memo’s integrity.”

Pérez, the youngest lawmaker in the California Senate, acknowledged that she and Torres had a prior personal relationship. She said L.A. TACO management asked them to limit their communication about six months ago, a request she said they honored.

A source close to Torres also rejected the ghostwriting allegations, arguing the veteran reporter would never allow another person to write under his byline. The insider claimed executives knew about the relationship as early as February and used it as a pretext to push Torres out amid internal disagreements over immigration coverage. The California Post has reached out to Torres for comment.

The outlet, however, said it had offered Torres a chance to leave on favorable terms, including a generous severance package and public support for his next venture.

“On his final day, Memo told us himself he was ready to go independent, and that it was a better fit for what he wanted to do,” the statement said. “We thought we left on good terms, and offered to publicly support his next chapter and give him a generous severance.”

L.A. TACO said Torres instead told followers he had been blindsided by the departure, fueling speculation that the newsroom was retreating from its ICE reporting.

“Memo built his name as a truth-teller and a community leader. But right now, a false narrative is being spread, and it’s dividing the very community he claims to serve,” the outlet said.

“Memo, you’ve always said you stand for the truth. Then tell it.”

Torres has disputed claims that he refused to take accountability for his work.
